title: Congress takes 24 of 37 district council chiefs in BJP-ruled Rajasthan; BJP wins 10
dek: The ruling BJP picked up five councils where it lacked a majority and snatched Churu through cross-voting, but lost the Chief Minister's home district of Bharatpur. Party leaders are now openly questioning the state leadership.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The opposition Congress won the chief's post in 24 of the 37 Rajasthan district councils (zila parishads) that elected their heads on Wednesday, extending its sweep of last week's rural local body elections in the state ruled by the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP won 10 Zila Pramukh posts, twice the five councils in which it had a majority, according to reports of the results.

The Bharat Adivasi Party won the tribal-majority districts of Banswara and Dungarpur, and Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal's Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) kept Nagaur. No independent was elected. Results for the remaining four of the state's 41 districts, Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar, are due in December.

## How the votes went

In the results of the panchayat samiti and zila parishad polls counted on 20 November, the Congress had won a clear majority in 23 of the 37 councils, the BJP in five and the RLP in one. On Wednesday, the elected members chose their chiefs.

The Congress held all but one of its 23 majority councils and added Salumbar, where no party had a majority, and Beawar, where the BJP had a majority but its candidate lost by one vote. In the Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's home district of Bharatpur, the Congress candidate won 17 votes to 14. The party's 21-year-old candidate Santosh Kumari, from a Scheduled Tribe community, was elected unopposed in Jaisalmer, as were Congress candidates in Dausa and Sawai Madhopur.

The BJP's biggest gain was Churu, where the Congress held 21 of 39 seats against the BJP's 17. The BJP's Kanika Singh, daughter-in-law of former minister Rajendra Rathore, won, indicating cross-voting by Congress members. The BJP also won Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Pratapgarh, where no party had a majority, besides its own majority councils of Ajmer, Pali, Jhalawar and Udaipur. Two contests, Didwana-Kuchaman and Dungarpur, ended in 14-14 ties and were decided by lottery, according to reports.

Arguments and jostling between rival party workers were reported in Jaipur, Bharatpur and Bhilwara.

## What the parties are saying

Former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot of the Congress congratulated the winners and said rural voters had voted against the BJP government's "misrule". Congress MP Rahul Kaswan said the government had made "numerous promises and none was fulfilled".

No formal statement from the state BJP on the Zila Pramukh results had been reported by Thursday afternoon. Several BJP leaders, speaking without being named, have described the rural results as a major embarrassment for a party in power, according to reports, blaming a range of factors from the bureaucracy's influence and weak co-ordination in the state leadership to discontent in parts of the party's upper-caste base over the University Grants Commission's equity guidelines. A leader close to the Chief Minister defended him, saying ministers had not backed his reform plans, according to the same reports. In September's urban local body polls, the BJP had held its own.

## Why it matters

Rajasthan's next Assembly election is due in 2028, but the results come as both national parties prepare for 2027 Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, where the Congress is negotiating a seat deal with the Samajwadi Party and the BJP is reviving its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal. Some BJP leaders at the centre want the party to address organisational gaps across states before then, according to reports.

The four remaining districts will choose their chiefs in December.
